abstract: This work studied the suitability of plantain peels as a friction material in the development of a brake pad. Ripe plantain peels used in this work was domestically sourced, washed, oven dried at a temperature of about 60oC. The dried plantain peels was pulverized using a locally made pulverizing machine then, sieved using a set of sieves arranged in descending order of fineness to obtain uniform particle size and carbonized in heat treatment furnace. The formulated brake pad composite was poured into a wooden mould 50 mm × 50 mm × 8 mm, placed in a hot platen press at temperature of about 180oC, at a molding pressure of about 15MPa and a curing time of 5 minutes. Post-heat treatment of the composites was performed in a hot air oven for a period of 4 hours at 180 °C. title: THERMO-MECHANICAL PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS OF DISC BRAKE USING VERTICAL AND INCLINED-SLOTTED BRAKE PADS UNDER TRANSIENT BRAKING
abstract: The orientation of brake pad slots significantly influences frictional heat generation, cooling behavior, and thermal stability in automotive disc brake systems under transient braking conditions. In this study, the transient thermal response of disc brakes equipped with vertical and inclined slotted non-asbestos organic (NAO) brake pads was investigated using experimental measurements and finite element analysis (FEA). Disc surface temperatures were measured at multiple radial locations under identical operating conditions. The results show that the vertical-slotted pad produced a lower peak disc temperature (≈283°C) than the inclined-slotted pad (≈315°C), corresponding to an approximate 10% reduction, while the experimental–numerical deviation remained within 5%. Radial temperature analysis revealed more uniform and speed-independent thermal profiles for the vertical-slot configuration, whereas inclined slots promoted localized heat accumulation and steeper thermal gradients. Cooling analysis indicated that the higher cooling rates observed for inclined slots were mainly due to their higher operating temperatures rather than improved heat dissipation efficiency. Overall, the results demonstrate that vertical-slot brake pads provide superior transient thermal stability, lower peak temperatures, and improved resistance to thermal localization under severe braking conditions.

title: Simulation and analysis of stick-slip vibration characteristics of brake discs for high-speed trains
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part K Journal of Multi-body Dynamics
abstract: To investigate stick-slip vibration between high-speed train brake discs and pads, a three-dimensional finite element model was developed in Abaqus using actual disc dimensions (brake disc material: 25Cr2MoVA; pad and backing plate material: copper-based powder metallurgy), simulating time-domain responses under various braking conditions via transient analysis. The stick-slip behavior of the brake pad was analyzed in the circumferential and radial directions at different positions, revealing the specific process on the contact surface. The vibration behavior of circular, triangular, and hexagonal brake pads at different angular velocities was compared to determine the optimal pad shape for suppressing stick-slip vibration. Circumferential analysis showed a vibration intensity distribution symmetric about the backing plate's central axis, with edge-proximal amplification: 3573 mm/s and 0.040 mm displacement at the friction entry side versus 2513 mm/s and 0.025 mm at the exit side. Radially, vibration intensity increased nonlinearly toward the rotation axis. The stick-slip mechanism initiated through localized sliding and propagated to full-surface transitions within 0.2-second cycles. Comparative evaluation identified the triangular pad as optimal, showing faster convergence (critical angular velocity 7.2 vs 7.3 rad/s for circular and 7.4 rad/s for hexagonal) and lower stabilized displacement (0.072 vs 0.080 mm and 0.077 mm). title: Tribological Characteristics of Periwinkle Shell/Raffia Palm Seed Reinforced Epoxy Hybrid Composites
abstract: Environmentally friendly and sustainable brake pad materials have attracted increasing attention due to the health and environmental concerns associated with asbestos-based friction materials. This study developed and characterized hybrid epoxy composites reinforced with periwinkle shell (PWS) and raffia palm seed (RPS) particles as potential eco-friendly brake pad materials. Unlike previous investigations that considered PWS or RPS individually, the present work examined their combined use in a hybrid system to evaluate the synergistic effects of agro-waste reinforcements on brake pad performance. Four composite formulations (Samples A–D) containing 4.41–17.71 wt.% PWS and 3.41–13.77 wt.% RPS were produced using epoxy resin as the matrix through molding and curing under a pressure of 18.25 kN/m². The composites were characterized by evaluating density, water absorption, hardness, wear depth, wear rate, and coefficient of friction. Results showed that increasing the reinforcement content significantly enhanced composite performance. Density increased from 2.60 to 3.28 g/cm³, while water absorption decreased from 0.1214% to 0.0388%. Hardness improved from 33.40 HV to 72 HV. title: Frictional Behavior and Torsional Vibration Implications of Advanced Drillstring Materials: Experimental Insights from Carbon Fiber, Titanium, and Aluminum
journal: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
abstract: Abstract Torsional stick–slip vibration continues to be one of the most destructive dynamic malfunctions in drilling operations, with a huge effect on drilling efficiency, tool life, and even operational safety. This paper presents an experimental investigation of the effect of the dynamic-to-static friction coefficient ratio (μd/μs) on torsional vibration behavior for three advanced drillstring materials: Carbon Fiber, Aluminum, and Titanium. Experiments were conducted using a scaled drilling vibration rig designed to replicate field-relevant torsional dynamics. The rotational responses at the bit were observed for μd/μs ratios of 0.2, 0.5, and 0.9 while maintaining constant top rotation speed (RPM). In addition to qualitative RPM analysis, a stick–slip severity index (SSI) was calculated for the quantitative analysis of torsional vibration intensity. Results show that increasing μd/μs ratio in all materials always reduces stick–slip severity. At low μd/μs, carbon fiber shows the highest SSI, which means severe stick–slip behavior, while aluminum shows moderate instability. Titanium exhibits the lowest SSI values and the most stable torsional response.

title: Tribocatalytic degradation of cationic dyes using Na₀.₄K₀.₁Bi₀.₅TiO₃: influence of friction pair materials and reactive species
abstract: Abstract This study explores the tribocatalytic activity of cationic dyes (Rhodamine B (RhB) and Methylene Blue (MB)) using Na 0.4 K 0.1 Bi 0.5 TiO 3 ( NKBT) as a catalyst under various conditions. The degradation efficiencies of RhB, MB, and binary (RhB + MB) dyes were examined, revealing that RhB exhibited higher degradation (~ 90%) compared to MB (~ 44%) at 600 rpm over 360 min. However, in the binary dye system, MB degraded more (~ 53%) than RhB (~ 9%), contrary to the results of individual dye degradation. The observed results may be attributed to the steric hindrance caused by the planar structure of MB molecules, which interferes with the Coulombic attraction between RhB dye and the catalyst surface, thereby reducing the degradation efficiency of RhB dye. Kinetic analysis showed rate constants of 0.00684 min − 1 , 0.00142 min − 1 , 0.00022 min − 1 , and 0.00208 min − 1 for RhB, MB, binary RhB, and binary MB, respectively. The effect of different friction pairs on RhB dye degradation was studied using polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) disc (homemade) with glass, polypropylene (PP), and PTFE beakers. The PTFE beaker-PTFE disc pair showed the highest degradation (~ 93%), followed by PP-PTFE (~ 89%) and glass-PTFE (~ 77%) at 600 rpm over 180 min. Optimal RhB dye degradation (~ 96%) was achieved in the PTFE beaker at 1000 rpm within 120 min.

title: The effect of post weld heat treatment (PWHT) on the mechanical properties (joint toughness) of friction stir weld joints of AA7000 using tool material of carbide tungsten (WC)
journal: Journal of Al-Farabi For Engineering Sciences
abstract: AA7075-T651 aluminum alloy is indispensable for weight-critical aerospace and automotive structures due to its exceptional strength-to-weight ratio, yet its weldability remains challenging via conventional fusion techniques. Friction stir welding (FSW) with a tungsten carbide (WC) tool offers a solid-state alternative that minimizes defects but induces microstructural degradation—particularly dissolution of strengthening precipitates and grain boundary alterations—severely reducing joint toughness, especially in the nugget zone (NZ). This work implemented post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) to restore precipitate distribution, systematically evaluating T6 (peak aging) and T7 (overaging) cycles on AA7075 FSW joints. Welding employed a WC tool (18 mm shoulder, 7.2 mm pin) at 800 RPM/90 mm/min. PWHT included solution treatment (480 °C/1 h) followed by T6 (120 °C/24 h) or T7 (105 °C/8 h + 170 °C/16 h) aging. Mechanical and microstructural characterization included Vickers hardness mapping, tensile testing (ASTM E8), Charpy V-notch impact tests (ASTM E23) with NZ-notched specimens, and OM/SEM fractography. Results indicated that T6 restored 94% of base metal tensile strength (538 MPa) but achieved only modest toughness (12.1 J). title: Adaptive Lateral Control of Vehicles under Abrupt and Nonuniform Tire–Road Friction
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This dataset accompanies the research manuscript entitled Adaptive Lateral Control of Vehicles under Abrupt and Nonuniform Tire–Road Friction. The study investigates adaptive model predictive control, lateral stability coordination, and constrained wheel-force allocation under abrupt and nonuniform tire–road friction conditions. The numerical evaluation comprises 88 physical scenarios, seven controllers, and 616 simulation runs using a four-wheel Fiala tire model. A separate numerical evaluation includes 144 simulations using a Dugoff combined-slip tire model. The deposited materials are intended to support the examination and reproducibility of the numerical findings, including conditional tracking performance, controller comparisons, failure outcomes, and model sensitivity. The primary evaluation focuses on a finite deterministic scenario set. The results do not constitute experimental vehicle validation or establish general performance superiority across all friction and driving conditions. The scope of reproducibility depends on the data, configurations, and analysis or simulation code included in this release. title: Self-enhanced optimization and transfer learning for accurate prediction and quality enhancement in friction stir welding
journal: International Journal of Cast Metals Research
abstract: Friction Stir Welding (FSW) improves material properties by refining the grain structure, which leads to enhanced strength and resistance to defects. This study proposes a novel Transfer Learning-based prediction model for Friction Stir Welding (TL-FSW) performance. Two datasets are employed to assess the capability of the GoogleNet with Transfer Learning (GNTL) model for predicting friction stir welding (FSW) performance. In the case of Aluminium Alloy (AA) 7075-T651, the model estimates surface roughness using key process variables. For AA6061, the model predicts the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) by utilising parameters such as rotational speed, welding speed and axial force. All three parameters are optimised via a Self-Enhanced Motherhood Optimisation (SE-MO) strategy to improve the accuracy of the prediction. The proposed TL-FSW model achieves lower prediction errors, with MAE values of 0.1678 and 0.1574 and MAPE values of 0.014 and 0.012 at 60% and 90% training data, respectively.

title: Robust and Wide-Range Friction Regulation via Interfacial Bridging-Promoted Hydration Switching in Phase-Separated Gels
abstract: Abstract Interfacial friction strongly influences materials performance, but achieving controllable friction with both high robustness and wide-range tunability remains difficult. In conventional friction regulation systems based on phase separations, rigid and incompatible hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces often cause interfacial cracking and poor stability. Here, inspired by the toughening mechanism of cartilage, we introduce amphiphilic bridging segments between hydrophilic and hydrophobic phases to construct an interfacial bridging nanophase-separated gel (IBNSGel) for robust friction control. This design transforms the fragile phase interface into a tough bridging interphase, suppresses aggregation, promotes uniform nanophase separation, and enhances interfacial stability during hydration-induced phase separation. Owing to this bridging effect, IBNSGel exhibits synergistic surface-bulk friction switching upon hydration: the surface forms a stable hydration layer for excellent lubrication, while the bulk hardens with higher modulus and lower damping, reducing conformal contact dissipation. As a result, this gel achieves stable, reversible, and wide-range coefficient of friction (CoF) switching during hydration–dehydration, with switching ratios of 150 at the macroscale and 330 at the microscale. title: Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation
abstract: Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. However, why contact electrification occurs remains a topic of hot debate, with ions, adsorbates, electrons and combinations thereof being ascribed the charge carriers. Irrespective of the charge carrier however, there must be a driving force inducing charge to separate and move from one surface to another. Herein, we demonstrate that electric fields, either applied externally or spontaneously generated at an interface can completely alter and even invert surface charge measured after contact electrification in polymer-polymer contact. Applying an external electric field allows the direct control of both magnitude and polarity static charge on dielectric polymers. These results are coupled to simulations that show the applied electric field is on the order of the fields generated by the flexoelectric effect - providing prima facie evidence of flexoelectric driven contact electrification.

title: Friction–wear behaviour of wood–plastic composites against WC–Co under low–temperature sliding conditions
abstract: This study investigated the friction and wear behaviour of wood–plastic composite (WPC) against WC–Co under dry and low–temperature conditions using 5 min pin–on–disc tests. The effects of normal load and rotational speed on the coefficient of friction (CoF), wear rate, and worn surface morphology were analysed. The results revealed that increasing normal load and rotational speed reduced the CoF but increased the wear rate. Compared with dry conditions, low–temperature conditions reduced the CoF by 4.2–10.7% and the wear rate by 23.2–57.3%. ANOVA identified normal load as the dominant factor affecting both responses. Test environment, normal load, rotational speed, and the load–speed interaction significantly affected the CoF, whereas only normal load and rotational speed significantly affected the wear rate. Low–temperature conditions restricted HDPE matrix softening and plastic flow and improved the stability of the wood flour–HDPE interface. This reduced material adhesion, wood flour pull–out, and interfacial damage, resulting in lower CoF and wear rate. These findings provide a clearer understanding of the tribological mechanisms of WPC under low–temperature sliding conditions.

title: Friction surfacing-based additive manufacturing of Ti–6Al–4V: process parameters, coating geometry, surface analysis, mechanical properties and corrosion behavior
abstract: Abstract In the present work, the solid state deposition of Ti–6Al–4V on grade 2 titanium substrates by friction surfacing was investigated. After initial parameter optimization to select adequate horizontal and vertical forward speeds, tests were conducted with rotational speeds of 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000 and 8000 rpm. The deposited material was subsequently characterized in terms of its overall geometry and surface texture, mechanical properties, microstructure and electrochemical corrosion resistance in Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS). Except for the coating obtained with 4000 rpm rotational speed, in all remaining cases deposits were relatively uniform and all coatings exhibited excellent bond strength—superior to the shear strength of the titanium substrate. The coatings exhibited elevated average hardness values ( $$\approx $$ 350 HV) and their microstructure was found to be composed mostly of needle-shaped $$\alpha $$ located at previous $$\beta $$ grain boundaries, with minor quantities of equiaxed $$\alpha $$ grains located near the substrate interface. No significant differences were noticed regarding the electrochemical behavior of the tested coatings, which exhibited similar corrosion resistance compared to the original base material, an indication of the reliability of the friction surfacing process for producing corrosion resistant coatings.

title: Evaluation of Tribological Behaviors of Lightweight Crosshead Materials in a Reciprocating Plunger Pump
abstract: Lightweight design is crucial for reducing inertial forces and vibrations in high-power-density reciprocating plunger pumps (RPPs). However, the tribological compatibility of lightweight alloys for crosshead–liner tribo-pairs is not well understood. This study systematically evaluates the friction and wear behaviors of six lightweight materials (TC4, TC4 (MAO), TC11, TC18, ZL108, and AlSi10Mg) sliding against HT250 gray cast iron under different lubrication conditions using an SRV IV tribometer. The results show that the lubrication regime significantly affects tribological performance. Water lubrication led to severe abrasive wear and high friction coefficients (0.75–0.91), while oil lubrication reduced friction to around 0.20 and promoted the formation of protective boundary films rich in P, S, and Zn. Material selection played a key role in wear mechanisms: aluminum alloys performed better under oil lubrication, whereas titanium alloys were more stable under water-lubricated conditions. MAO treatment on TC4 improved wear resistance, reducing the wear weight to less than 0.3 mg under oil lubrication by creating a strong ceramic oxide layer. Negative wear rates in lower specimens indicated material transfer from the upper specimen to the lower specimen. Based on performance metrics, the TC4-MAO/Shell 220 combination is recommended for lightweight crosshead applications. This study offers insights and guidelines for material selection to enhance the reliability and efficiency

title: Process Parameter Optimization in Refill Friction Stir Spot Welding of 6061-T6 Aluminum Alloy and AZ31B-H24 Magnesium Alloy Dissimilar Joints
journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing

title: Haptic properties of polymeric materials: link between human perception and microstructure
abstract: Abstract Haptic properties, i.e. the tactile sensations experienced when touching a material, play a crucial role in product acceptance, user experience, and functional performance across diverse industries. Polymeric materials dominate applications where haptics matter, from consumer packaging and automotive interiors to medical devices and textiles. This review discusses the relationship between polymer structure and haptic perception, with the aim of designing materials with targeted tactile properties. Fields addressed herein are molecular architecture and formulation strategies for precise control over haptic attributes including friction, roughness, compliance, and thermal sensation. By bridging fundamental polymer science with psychophysical perception, this review offers practical guidance for developing polymeric materials with optimized haptic performance. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Experimental protocols used in tactile perception of materials: a mini review
abstract: Tactile perception plays a central role in how humans evaluate and interact with materials, influencing perceived roughness, softness, friction, warmth, wetness, comfort, quality, and usability. In recent years, experimental studies on tactile perception have expanded across diverse material systems, including textiles, synthetic fibers, plastics, wood, building materials, soft rubbers, textured surfaces, and haptic overlays. However, the experimental protocols used across these studies remain highly varied. This mini-review examines recent experimental approaches adopted in tactile perception studies of materials, with emphasis on work published within approximately the last 5 years. We identified common methodological strategies, including psychophysical rating scales, forced-choice and pairwise-comparison tasks, tactile-only and visual–tactile testing, active-touch standardization, instrumented material characterization, and multisensory or haptic-interface protocols. By comparing these approaches, the review highlights how differences in material selection, sensory access, exploratory movement, subjective rating methods, and physical characterization influence the interpretation of tactile perception data. title: Comparative Study of the Microstructure, Local Elemental Composition, Microhardness, and Dry-Sliding Friction Behavior of Co-Cr-W, Fe-Mn-C, and Fe-Cr-Ni-Mn GTAW Deposits on 09G2S Steel

abstract: The incorporation of graphene-based materials into powder-based manufacturing processes offers opportunities to tailor material processing and performance. title: Finite Element Analysis of Drone Impact on a Rotating Aircraft Engine Fan: Sensitivity to Blade Material and Impact Velocity
journal: Modelling—International Open Access Journal of Modelling in Engineering Science
abstract: An explicit finite element study examined the sensitivity of a rotating aircraft-engine fan to blade material and drone impact velocity. A complete 20-blade rotor and a deformable, equivalent-material quadcopter were modelled in ANSYS/LS-DYNA. Ti-6Al-4V, Ti-6242 and AA2024-T3 blades were assessed at 30, 60 and 100 m/s with an initial fan angular velocity of 283 rad/s. Nine frictional simulations and one Ti-6Al-4V frictionless case at 100 m/s were evaluated using stress, equivalent plastic strain, directional displacement, erosion and energy histories. Ti-6Al-4V produced the lowest maximum blade plastic strain at each velocity; AA2024-T3 values were 11.6–26.9 times greater despite lower equivalent stress. No fan elements were deleted, whereas drone deletion occurred in every case. The maximum-history reduction in surviving-drone kinetic energy increased with velocity, but the highest velocity did not produce the largest plastic strain in every material. Including friction increased maximum plastic strain by a factor of 6.46 in the sensitivity case. title: Evaluation of Fretting Wear of Contact Surfaces of Composite Material-Aircraft Alloy in Nominally Stationary Joints of Aircraft Structures
abstract: The article examines and analyzes the use of composite materials, such as carbon fiber-reinforced plastic (CFRP) and glass fiber-reinforced plastic (GFRP), in new-generation aircraft. Comparative studies were conducted on these composite materials alongside aviation alloys based on aluminum, titanium, and steel. It was determined that contact interfaces in nominally stationary joints suffer significant damage due to vibrational loads—stemming from aircraft engines and normal operations—a phenomenon classified as fretting corrosion. The study found that Al-CFRP/GFRP contact leads to the catastrophic degradation of friction surfaces caused by the formation of hard Al2O3 oxides. Ti-CFRP/GFRP contact is the most common configuration in new-generation aircraft; notably, the wear resistance of the composite materials is 6–20 times higher than that of the titanium alloy, owing to the inherent properties of titanium and its susceptibility to wear. Furthermore, the article analyzes surface processing and protection methods for titanium components aimed at enhancing the durability and wear resistance of these contact pairs.

title: Micromechanical signature of representative volume conditions in granular materials: Particle-shape effects and column-like load-bearing structures
abstract: Representative volume conditions in coarse granular materials are investigated using three-dimensional Contact Dynamics simulations of drained triaxial compression tests. Dense assemblies of spherical particles and ballast-like polyhedral grains reconstructed from digitized railway ballast particles are compared to assess how particle shape influences the transition from finite-size-dominated behavior to representative bulk response. The nominal system-size ratio 𝛼 n o m = 𝑊 0 / 𝑑 m a x is varied from 3 to 16. The results show that small systems exhibit pronounced stress fluctuations, lower internal coordination, broader normal force distributions, and strong sensitivity of the force-bearing network to specimen size. As 𝛼 n o m increases, macroscopic quantities and micromechanical descriptors progressively stabilize. For both particle shapes, the macroscopic response becomes only weakly dependent on specimen size for 𝛼 n o m ≥ 8 . Particle shape strongly modifies the mechanisms of stress transmission. Polyhedral grains develop higher critical-state shear strength, larger contact anisotropy, and stronger tangential force anisotropy than spheres, reflecting enhanced interlocking and frictional mobilization. However, the apparent transition toward representative behavior occurs over a comparable nominal size range for both particle shapes. A dedicated filtering procedure is introduced to identify column-like structures, defined as unbranched chains of strongly loaded particles.

abstract: This paper establishes the formal fluid-mechanical and quantitative laws governing the degradation of sub-spatial information, the mechanical stability thresholds of free nucleons, and the structural limits of material thermal conduction within a crystalline 3D superfluid. By evaluating the continuous energy leakage of a photon wavefront into the cosmic microwave background (CMB), we prove that EPR entanglement is mechanically non-infinite, possessing an absolute dimensional decay parameter locked to the lattice friction coefficient. Furthermore, we derive the exact spatial volume gradient of the neutron's external torsional stress cloud (Vstress ≈ 2.37 × 10-43 m3), physically demonstrating why high-velocity ram-pressure and sub-spatial Venturi exhaust venting into adjacent proton sinks dictate radioactive decay rates and nuclear binding energy. Finally, we mathematically model thermal energy transfer, proving that solid-state conduction efficiency is governed by structural shielding thresholds that isolate the 4D sub-spatial channel circuit against the universal cosmostatic base pressure P0.

title: Reorienting Indigenous Heritage for Socioenvironmental Justice
abstract: Abstract This article presents a study of the archaeological ruins of Tiwanaku and Quilmes in the south-central Andes as spaces of equivocation at the intersection of diverging human–nature and past–present ontologies. Drawing on multisited archaeological ethnography, the research reveals the underlying struggles for Indigenous heritage rights and self-determination through discursive–material juxtapositions, frictional materialities, and multiple temporalities. Three lines of inquiry are examined: (a) the modern–colonial origins of dominant configurations of heritage rights in the Andes, (b) the failures of development projects aimed at the “rehabilitation” of native technologies and knowledge, and (c) the pluriversal becoming of Indigenous heritage from the ruins of multicultural development. The findings offer a critical counterpoint to rights-based narratives and consent-seeking approaches that objectify heritage and communities within hegemonic conservation and development regimes. Alternative forms of political subjectivity and socionatural configurations enable an assessment of the entangled environmental and decolonial dimensions of heritage, indigeneity, and rights.

title: Topological Reconfiguration in Sheared Granular Assemblies: Non-Dissipative Mechanism and Its Irreversible Characteristics
abstract: Granular materials exhibit pronounced macroscopic irreversible deformations during shearing, which mainly contributes to frictional sliding dissipation in the conventional thermodynamic frameworks. This study aims to investigate the non-dissipative microscopic mechanisms governing macroscopic irreversibility of granular materials. title: A review of tribo-mechanical characteristics of nickel and aluminum-based metal matrix composites
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part B Journal of Engineering Manufacture
abstract: Metal matrix composites (MMCs) are extensively used materials for adverse operating conditions, where the good properties of one material cannot cope with the operating conditions. Most studies showed the matrix as metallic, and the reinforcements could be metal, polymers, ceramics, or even hybrids. Now-a-days, MMCs are widely adopted for the fabrication of many components like vehicle bodies, aeroplane bodies, machines, weapons, etc. These components encounter frictional resistance from several sources. To assess and select a suitable material for the fabrication of these components, the tribological characteristics of these materials need to be analyzed. These components also need to withstand severe stresses from numerous sources, like impact loads, thermal stresses, etc., so mechanical properties are also important. The principal objective of this paper is to provide a detailed description of the tribological and mechanical characteristics of MMCs with different combinations of matrices and reinforcements. This study aims to explore the tribological and mechanical properties of Metal Matrix Composites (MMCs), realizing various matrix and reinforcement combinations. It highlights that MMCs are crucial for applications requiring resistance to friction, stress, and impact, necessitating analysis of both tribological and mechanical characteristics for material selection.

title: Tribological and mechanical properties of Al/MoS 2 composite strips fabricated via accumulative roll bonding process
abstract: Aluminum matrix composites reinforced with solid lubricants have attracted considerable attention for tribological applications owing to their potential to combine high specific strength with improved friction and wear behavior. In the present work, Al-5 wt.% MoS 2 composite sheets and monolithic aluminum sheets were successfully fabricated through the accumulative roll bonding (ARB) process up to eight passes. The influence of ARB passes on the microstructure, crystallite size, hardness, tensile properties, friction coefficient, and wear behavior of both materials was systematically investigated. Microstructural characterization revealed a significant grain refinement and homogeneous distribution of MoS 2 within the aluminum matrix after repeated ARB processing. The crystallite size decreased progressively with increasing ARB passes, leading to an increase in hardness and tensile strength for both materials. Tribological investigations showed that the incorporation of MoS. reduced the coefficient of friction compared with monolithic aluminum. title: Deterministic analytical modeling of coupled electrical conductivity and tribological behavior in Cu Zn Ni Si alloys
abstract: In this study, the combined influence of material composition, load, and sliding velocity on the properties of wear and electrical properties of copper–zinc–nickel–silicon alloys is investigated. An approach based on deterministic modeling is recommended to predict the influence of zinc content and nickel-silicon reinforced material under various loads. Wear behavior and electrical transport characteristics are correlated through the material composition and resistivity relationship. From these results, it can be observed that there is a clear trend of increasing electrical conductivity with an increase in the amount of the alloy to up to 121 percent of the IACS value. Wear is maintained at the level of 10⁻ 5 mm 3 / (Nm), meaning there is consistency of performance at loads between 5 and 20 newtons. Higher loads lead to higher wear as well as higher temperatures, while higher sliding velocities reduce friction and surface interaction. It is believed by the suggested deterministic model that the composition of the alloy plays an important role in determining the electric conductivity as well as wear, whereas the load applied and the sliding speed determine the frictional and thermal response. The proposed approach can be used to evaluate the behavior of the alloy through a repeatable methodology. However, it is limited to simulation-based verification within a specific range of parameters.

title: Heat transfer enhancement of supercritical CO2 in a novel triangular − prism rib tube based on field synergy principle
journal: International Journal of Heat and Fluid Flow
abstract: Supercritical CO 2 (sCO 2 ) Brayton cycle can address the challenges of high-temperature corrosion of materials and improve the power generation efficiency to over 50%. However, sCO 2 flow in horizontal tubes is prone to exhibit low heat transfer efficiency due to circumferentially non-uniform heat transfer. Conventional heat transfer enhancement (HTE) methods often lead to excessive frictional loss. In this work, triangular-prism rib tube with local arrangement is proposed to enhance heat transfer and decrease frictional loss. The results show that local ribs effectively decrease the top wall temperature ( T w ) and improve the heat transfer. For a fixed rib distribution range, the tube with a circumferential spacing of 30° makes that the temperature difference between the upper and lower levels is reduced to 17 K, heat transfer coefficient ( HTC ) rises by 38%, and friction factor ( ƒ ) only increases by 0.03. For a fixed circumferential spacing, the value of performance evaluation criterion ( PEC ) in the tube with a distribution range of 360° is 41% higher than that of the smooth tube.

title: The Buy-in Effect: When Increasing Initial Effort Encourages Follow-Through

abstract: Behavioral interventions often focus on reducing friction to encourage behavior change. In contrast, we provide evidence that adding initial friction to a sign-up process can increase follow-through behavior. In a field experiment with a state department of transportation ([Formula: see text]), we test whether adding modest friction during sign-up for a carpool platform increases usage. Although a more effortful sign-up process leads to 25% fewer sign-ups, overall usage increases. Importantly, these results were only partly explained by selection: Using an intent-to-treat analysis, participants with a more effortful sign-up process took 1.6 times more carpool trips per week over four months, leading to more overall trips despite fewer users. In a second experiment with online task work, participants with more effortful sign-up were 37% more likely to return the next day and completed more work overall. These results suggest that adding friction may be an overlooked strategy when follow-through, rather than initial uptake, is the primary goal. title: Surface microtextures on medical Zr-based metallic glasses via femtosecond laser processing: Optimization and performance
abstract: Zr-based bulk metallic glasses (Zr-BMGs) have attracted considerable attention for biomedical applications owing to their unique amorphous structure, excellent corrosion resistance, and high hardness. abstract: Background The national pavilion model, epitomised by the Venice Biennale, functions as an internal cultural border that aligns artistic production with state sovereignty and Eurocentric universality. abstract: Abstract Cold rolling is one of the most widely applied metal-forming processes, where strip flatness is a critical quality requirement affecting downstream manufacturability, dimensional accuracy and product performance. abstract: In this preliminary investigation, a double-layered AZ91 magnesium structure was developed using solid-state friction stir additive manufacturing (FSAM) by varying the tool rotation speed and traverse speed. title: Learning to Live with Low-tech: User Experience of Self-Built Low-Tech Systems in the Home
abstract: Sustainability discourse increasingly promotes simple, repairable, useful “low‑tech” alternatives, yet little is known about how such systems are experienced over time in everyday life. We investigated how user experience evolves during early use of low-tech systems through a two‑month participatory citizen program. Twenty‑six participants built and used 5 systems at home. We retrospectively analyzed their experience with the UX Curve method. Findings reveal recurring practical challenges, mismatches between expected and perceived utility, and material or aesthetic limitations that often undermine engagement. Participants also reported experiences grounded in eudaimonic qualities—autonomy, competence, alignment with personal values—and friction that made effort feel meaningful rather than burdensome. We argue that scaling low‑tech alternatives depends less on optimizing systems than on designing resources for action that support appropriation, learning, and distributed innovation. Based on these insights, we derive implications for HCI to support low‑tech as empowering, ecological experiences that challenge technocratic framings of sustainability.

title: Syllogistic Critique of Modernity: Systemic Decoupling, Physical Limits, and the Modern Koan
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This whitepaper presents a formal collaborative framework analyzing the structural contradictions of late modernity through the lens of systemic decoupling—the process by which institutional, financial, and technological systems abstract themselves from physical boundaries, thermodynamic realities, and finite biophysical inputs. Operating under the unstated systemic constraint "You are not to know you are imperfect," modern optimization vectors are shown to be fundamentally unstable hallucinations that generate compounding environmental and physical debts. To bridge this macro-structural decoupling with immediate human experience, the paper introduces a contemporary social koan: “Keep my budget sad.And my loneliness at bay.” This paradox serves as a precise conceptual bridge, mapping the internal friction of the individual trapped within modern economic architectures where human connection has been commodified, leaving the subject exposed directly to the dual forces of material scarcity and emotional isolation. Through a synthesis of formal syllogistic critiques across global philosophical nodes, this paper details the mechanics of technological entropy export, evaluates boundary stress-tests like generative model collapse, and outlines design parameters for re-anchoring human infrastructure within absolute planetary boundaries.

title: Dielectric Properties of Silicone Resins from Substituent Effects to High-Temperature Structural Evolution
abstract: Abstract Silicone resins are highly desirable matrix materials for high-temperature wave transparent applications. title: Confined‐Space Self‐Assembly of Nano‐HNS Into Hierarchical Micro‐Nano Structured Microspheres for Selective Stimuli Sensitization and Passivation
abstract: To address the balance between reactivity and safety in nano-HNS, this study presents a green composite molding strategy that facilitates the self-assembly of nano-HNS into micro-nano-structured microspheres within confined spaces. This approach utilizes confined spaces to precisely control the morphology and size of the resultant microspheres. The effects of process parameters on the morphology and size of microspheres were systematically investigated, and the underlying formation mechanisms were elucidated. Comprehensive characterizations encompassing morphology, crystal structure, mechanical sensitivity, thermal behavior, and impact properties were conducted. The results demonstrate that the synthesized HNS microspheres possess high sphericity, an average particle size of 224.2 µm, and exhibit favorable fluidity and bulk density. This approach effectively reduces the mechanical sensitivity of the material while preserving the crystal structure and thermal stability of HNS-IV (impact sensitivity: 12 J vs. 20 J; friction sensitivity: 216 N vs. 240 N). Furthermore, it enhances the initial sensitivity to short duration shock, as evidenced by reductions in the 50% and 99.9% initiation voltages by 18 and 48 V, respectively. This approach facilitates the synergistic stimulation of selective sensitization and passivation. This methodology is straightforward and applicable, providing a versatile and eco-friendly approach for the multi-structural modification of nano-HNS.

abstract: The bond-slip behavior at the brick-mortar interface plays a pivotal role in the long-term structural integrity of ancient masonry pagodas. journal: Proceedings of The International Conference on New Trends in Social Sciences
abstract: This article develops a formal model of identity as a multi-dimensional system of value. Contemporary social theory has examined identity through recognition, capital, redistribution, narrative and justification, and this article brings selected insights into a jointly specified account of how heterogeneous forms of value are structured, allocated and transformed. abstract: The role of tires in vehicle dynamics has evolved from passive support elements to active sources of information. abstract: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) convert low-frequency and irregular mechanical energy into electrical energy for self-powered sensors, wearable electronics, Internet-of-Things devices and distributed energy systems. Although major advances have been made in triboelectric materials, surface engineering and device architectures, the mechanical excitation applied during TENG testing remains an important source of experimental variability. title: DexNinja: Learning Robust Dexterous Cutting Policy with a Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Engine
abstract: Cutting a piece of food looks effortless in human hands. For a robot, however, every cut is a high-contact interaction with a deformable, elasto-plastic object whose behavior changes with pose, contact mode, and cutting stage. Collecting real-world data is expensive and wasteful: each trial typically contaminates or damages the food, so obtaining scalable real world data for dexterous cutting is expensive and difficult. Simulation is an appealing alternative, but a large sim-to-real gap exists in both physics and perception. This gap is especially severe for topology-changing interactions like cutting, where small errors in contact, friction, or material and elasticity responses quickly compound. We evaluate \textsc{DexNinja} on a dexterous food-slicing task and show that (1) with tens of real demonstrations and hundreds of augmented simulator data, the success rate could reach more than 60\%. title: Enhancement of wear resistance in Mo-based composites through moderate addition of (Hf0.25Ta0.25Nb0.25Ti0.25)C high entropy ceramics
abstract: Molybdenum alloys offer excellent high-temperature properties but suffer from poor wear resistance, which limits their use in severe friction and high-load environments. In this study, different concentrations of (Hf 0.25 Ta 0.25 Nb 0.25 Ti 0.25 )C High entropy carbides (HECs) were doped into the pure molybdenum (Mo), and their wear resistance was investigated and compared with pure Mo under different loads, utilizing XRD, SEM, TEM, EBSD, surface hardness testing, and surface profilometry for comprehensive characterization. Surprisingly, at a load of 30 N and 40 N, the 3% HECs doped sample exhibits a lower wear rate of 0.75 × 10 -7 mm 3 /N·m and 1.37 × 10 -7 mm 3 /N·m, which reduced by 52.8% and 28% compared to pure Mo samples. However, when the load increases to 50 N, the wear resistance of HECs doped samples is even worse than that of pure Mo sample. The superior wear resistance under low loads is attributed to the dispersion strengthening effect induced by HECs doping, which enhances the surface hardness and increases the dislocation density. In contrast, the deterioration in wear resistance under high loads is attributed to the detachment and fragmentation of ceramic particles, which transition from reinforcing agents to abrasive third-body wear particles, thereby accelerating material removal. The strategy proposed herein holds substantial promise for enhancing the wear resistance of molybdenum and its alloys.

title: Current-driven Magnetic Skyrmions for Encoding/Storing Information: Manipulation and Dynamics in Nanoscale Structures
abstract: This dissertation investigates the dynamics of current-driven magnetic skyrmions, topological solitons in magnetic materials with broken spatial inversion symmetry, for low-power spintronic applications like racetrack memory and multilevel data storage. Skyrmions’ small size and low driving current requirements make them promising information carriers. The research examines skyrmion motion under driving currents, pinning effects, and thermal fluctuations, using numerical simulations (Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation), analytical studies (Thiele equation), and theoretical modeling to design novel data storage devices. The study analyzes skyrmion motion amidst pinning potentials from material imperfections. Simulations reveal that thermal fluctuations vary with damping: acting as a frictional force at low damping or a driving force aiding depinning at high damping. The Thiele equation quantifies this, though its accuracy wanes at low temperatures with pinning. The skyrmion Hall angle, influenced by current and pinning, provides insights for ambient-condition devices. These findings underpin a proposed multilevel data storage device, where controlled current positions skyrmions at pinning sites for high-density, low-power encoding. abstract: In this study, the effects of resin type (epoxy and unsaturated polyester) and reinforcement ratio (40–70 wt%) on the dynamic behavior of waste Astragalus bark (Astragalus gummifer – AG)-reinforced polymer composites were experimentally investigated. abstract: Purpose This paper aims to focus on the hydrodynamic stability of steady-state natural convection inside a vertical flat porous microchannel. The main objective is to investigate the transition conditions from stable to unstable flow under the Boussinesq approximation, explicitly incorporating velocity slip and temperature jump boundary conditions at the channel walls. title: Green Taxation under GST 2.0: Incentivising Renewable Energy and Circular Economy Enterprises
journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
first_author: Anil Kumar, Bindu Bharti, Prof. Leena Sharad Shimpi
abstract: Purpose: This paper examines how India’s GST 2.0 reform treats renewable energy and circular economy enterprises, and identifies the frictions in input tax credit (ITC), rate structure, refunds and compliance that weaken the fiscal signal for green investment. Methodology: The study combines a doctrinal analysis of the CGST Act, the Finance Act 2025, rate notifications and key judicial and advance-ruling decisions; stylised cost arithmetic on credit denial, composite rates and inverted duty; a comparative review of Germany’s zero-rating of photovoltaic systems and China’s refund-based support for resource recycling; and a synthesis of OECD, World Bank, NITI Aayog and peer-reviewed literature. It is a secondary, document-based study and does not use primary survey data. Findings: Five findings emerge: (1) ITC eligibility for renewable assets remains contested and was narrowed by the Finance Act 2025; (2) the cut to 5 per cent on renewable devices leaves a residual rate mismatch and exposure to inverted duty; (3) compliance costs fall disproportionately on small firms, and refund claims, the statutory remedy for inversion, are associated with markedly higher compliance cost; (4) GST draws no distinction between virgin and recycled materials, weakening circular business models; and (5) fiscal instruments have lagged India’s physical renewable build-out. Drawing on public-finance principles, the paper argues that reforms restoring VAT neutrality should precede concessional rates.

title: Regenerative braking control for electric vehicles with battery and safety constraints
abstract: Regenerative braking recovers energy while slowing an electric vehicle. Its contribution is limited by battery charge acceptance, motor capability, and tire grip. When the battery charging limit falls, friction braking may need to replace the lost regenerative torque. Different actuator response times can then cause a shortfall in total braking torque. This mini-review examines how battery limits and brake control are coordinated. It compares rule-based, fuzzy, predictive, and learning-based methods, with attention to actuator response and validation. It also examines dual-motor torque allocation and one-pedal control, using documented production functions as examples. Immediate battery protection is distinguished from long-term battery aging. The reviewed studies show why lower charging current alone does not establish a battery-life benefit. A key control task is to manage changes in regenerative capability during braking. Predicting these changes may help prepare the friction brakes, but the current battery and tire limits must still be respected. The review proposes combined battery and road test cases. It also defines torque-deficit measures for assessing brake transitions. Future studies should report recovered energy alongside deceleration, wheel slip, actuator delay, and battery response under matched test conditions.

title: Hybrid Sliding-Mode-Based Wheel Slip Control for Brake-by-Wire Vehicles with In-Wheel Motors
abstract: Sliding-mode control (SMC) is valued in automotive applications for its robustness and its low computational cost, although chattering remains a practical obstacle. Higher-order and adaptive formulations reduce chattering, but each carries limitations that may restrict their use in wheel slip control. This paper presents a hybrid low-level controller that combines a first-order sliding-mode (FOSM) term with a proportional–integral (PI) term acting on the same slip error. The two branches are weighted by a hyperbolic tangent function, so that the FOSM term governs the response towards the reference slip and the PI term governs it within a narrow band around the reference. Because the weighting is continuous, the transfer between branches introduces no step change in the torque demand. The controller is embedded in a three-level brake-by-wire architecture with series brake blending between in-wheel motors and friction brakes. The study uses an experimentally validated 14-DOF vehicle model and proposes a benchmarking procedure for comparison against a velocity-scheduled PI baseline. The results suggest improved slip tracking of the braking manoeuvre.

title: Event-Driven Safe Control of a Black-Box Balancing Wheel with Friction-Gated Actuation
abstract: Commercial balancing wheels are closed systems: an internal controller keeps the board upright, and a rider steers by shifting weight and twisting the hips. We augment a one-wheel with a lead-screw weight shift for longitudinal motion and a reaction wheel for yaw. The reaction wheel stores limited momentum, so a turn is a sequence of torque pulses, and whether a pulse rotates the body depends on static friction at the tire contact. From a 24-pulse torque sweep on one surface we fit a two-part model that gives the probability that a pulse rotates the body, treating the breakaway torque as random, and the rotation angle when it does; at maximum torque the posterior engagement probability is 0.54 (90% credible interval 0.24-0.84). The weight shift is modeled as a rate- limited input with a measured speed gain and an assumed first-order response, which predicts stopping distances four times those of a direct-force model. These models drive an event-triggered supervisor that schedules pulses by expected heading improvement, brakes when the predicted braking path would leave the safe set, tightens margins for model uncertainty, and updates the friction estimate online. In simulation on 500 plants drawn from the fitted models, the robust supervisor completed 92.6% of missions with 1.8% safety violations and 1.6% safe aborts, versus 84.0% and 7.2% for a supervisor using mean models and 1.8% and 20.4% for a baseline that ignores friction. title: Introduction
abstract: The study of human performance on a bicycle is not a recent phenomenon. Indeed, the cycle ergometer has been a cornerstone of physiological research for over a century, evolving from the rudimentary friction-braked devices of the late 19th century to the sophisticated laboratory instruments of today ( Vandewalle & Driss, 2015 ). This long history provided the foundation to investigate the fundamental principles of exercise physiology, many of which were first articulated by Nobel laureate A.V. Hill. His pioneering work distinguishing aerobic from anaerobic metabolism and defining concepts such as “maximum O 2 intake” established the theoretical questions that the ergometer was uniquely positioned to answer in the exercising human ( Bassett, 2002 ). The subsequent standardisation and widespread adoption of laboratory ergometry laid the groundwork for an explosion of research. In recent decades, the technological leap from stationary ergometers to mobile, on-bike power meters has coincided with a dramatic growth in scientific publications, rising from 855 in 1985 to over 18,000 in 2024 ( Figure 1.1 ).

abstract: Real-world driving tests reflect vehicle performance in everyday use, but extracting energy conversion data from extensive measurements remains challenging. The study compared a hybrid electric vehicle and a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle, with the latter operated in charge-sustaining mode, against three conventional vehicles in real-world driving tests. The moving average window method transformed second-by-second measurements into tens of thousands of quasi-trip samples representing diverse driving scenarios. Using the linear correlation between slope CO2 emissions and slope height in the data window samples, a linear regression-based parameter identification method was proposed to infer the total braking energy recovery ratios of the hybrid vehicles, exploring a way to assess vehicle energy conversion characteristics on the roads. The tested hybrid vehicles exhibited lower urban CO2 emissions and, under mountainous and aggressive driving conditions, greater advantages primarily attributable to braking energy recovery. However, under the tested conditions, the hybrid vehicles showed no significant advantage in engine thermal efficiency over the conventional counterpart equipped with a downsized turbocharged engine. Engine downsizing may contribute to efficient engine operation, offering some of the efficiency benefits comparable to those achieved through optimized engine–motor torque distribution in hybrid vehicles.

abstract: With the increasing global energy demand and the advancement of carbon neutrality goals, efficient and low-carbon power systems have attracted extensive attention in heavy-duty engine research. title: Node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing and carbon-responsive control of electrified railways for emission reduction and tertiary reserves
abstract: The decarbonization of electrified transportation reshapes the interaction between power systems and mobile energy loads. As a key component of this sector, electrified railways draw large, geographically distributed traction loads whose emissions are governed by the power system’s spatiotemporally varying carbon intensity (CI). However, existing carbon tracing methods typically use spatially uniform emission factors, obscuring nodal carbon intensity (CI) differences. Consequently, long-distance trains cannot perceive or exploit spatial carbon heterogeneity when allocating traction power along their routes. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a unified framework that transforms heterogeneous railway fleets into active, carbon-responsive resources within the power system. First, a node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing method integrates Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDF) with dynamic train-node mapping, enabling real-time quantification of the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) experienced by mobile loads. Building upon this, a two-stage hierarchical coordinated control strategy is formulated, embedding dynamic NCI signals into an online receding-horizon predictive controller to achieve joint carbon minimization and tertiary reserve. The controller autonomously executes spatiotemporal load shifting by dynamically regulating traction and braking power to avoid high-carbon zones while maintaining schedule adherence. abstract: This study experimentally investigates the performance, emission, energy, and exergy characteristics of six fuels in a two-cylinder, air-cooled, two-stroke unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) engine, using neat gasoline (G100) as the reference fuel. Experiments were conducted at shaft speeds of 3250, 3750, 4500, 5250, and 6250 rpm under matched speed–load conditions. Fuel consumption, exhaust-gas temperature, excess-air ratio, gaseous emissions, and first- and second-law thermodynamic performance were evaluated. The inclusion of G100 enabled the effects of the oxygenated additives to be quantified directly. At 5250 rpm, G90E10 reduced BSFC by 0.73% relative to G100 while increasing energy and exergy efficiencies by 1.69% and 1.61%, respectively. title: Surrogate-Assisted Multi-Objective Optimization of Engine-Level Pneumatic Assistance for Arctic Diesel Generators
abstract: Diesel generators remain indispensable for supplying reliable electricity in isolated Arctic microgrids, where harsh environmental conditions, high fuel transportation costs, and stringent emission requirements motivate improvements in engine performance and environmental sustainability. This study proposes and validates a unified, surrogate-assisted tri-objective optimization framework to calibrate the engine operation of a pneumatically assisted CAT 3516 diesel generator under representative Arctic conditions at Raglan Mine, Canada. The optimization focuses on engine-level pneumatic assistance, while compressed air generation, storage, and distribution are outside the scope of the study. The framework integrates high-fidelity Diesel-RK simulations, adaptive Sobol sampling, Gaussian Process surrogate modeling with predictive uncertainty, global sensitivity analysis, deterministic multi-objective optimization, SIMUS-based Pareto ranking, and independent high-fidelity validation. We optimized three engine-control variables (start of injection, compressor pressure ratio, and fuel mass per cycle) simultaneously to maximize brake power while minimizing brake-specific fuel consumption and NOx emissions. title: The Application of Waste Coal Fly Ash as a Support for a Heterogeneous Catalyst for Biodiesel Production and a Comparison with the Engine Characteristics Using a Homogeneous Catalyst
abstract: Abstract Coal fly ash is a waste product of coal-fired boiler combustion. The fly ash consists of fine glass microspheres with a relatively large surface area. This study aims to synthesize catalysts using waste coal fly ash as a support and calcine them with alkaline catalysts. Fly ash with a large surface area was synthesized using sodium methoxide to prepare a heterogeneous catalyst, which was then used to transesterify palm oil to produce biodiesel. Subsequently, engine performance and exhaust emissions from biodiesel combustion were evaluated. The experimental results indicate that biodiesel prepared with the heterogeneous catalyst exhibited lower fuel consumption and brake-specific fuel consumption (BSFC) than biodiesel prepared with the homogeneous catalyst, and it had a higher brake thermal efficiency. The emission concentrations of CO, CO2, and NOX are higher in biodiesel produced with homogeneous catalysts, whereas the O2 emission concentration from biodiesel prepared with a heterogeneous catalyst is lower than that of homogeneous biodiesel. Moreover, the biodiesel produced using a heterogeneous catalyst consisting of coal fly ash containing sodium methoxide appeared to have a lower excess air ratio and heating value, while exhibiting a higher exhaust gas temperature and fuel/air equivalence ratio. Using waste coal fly ash to synthesize a heterogeneous catalyst improves biodiesel properties, thereby advancing the circular economy.

abstract: Abstract Reactivity Controlled Compression Ignition (RCCI) engines are a promising way to decarbonize the internal combustion engine industry. Despite this extensive literature covering dual‐fuel setups, a critical knowledge gap persists regarding the steady‐state combustion behavior of highly specific, waste‐derived oxygenated lipids when paired directly with carbon‐free LRFs. To address this gap, the current study focuses on the waste‐to‐wealth principle of utilizing Milk Scum biodiesel and mineral diesel (as a High‐Reactivity Fuel) and hydrogen (as an LRF) to achieve the minimum carbon‐based emissions. Experimentally, performance and emissions were measured using a constant‐rpm diesel engine with a compression ratio of 18, fuel injection pressure of 500 bar, fuel injection time of 23 bTDC, and common‐rail direct‐injected (B10, B15, and B20) and port‐injected hydrogen (0.077 and 0.121 kg/h) at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% engine loads. The measurements indicate that the RCCI optimality (0.121 kg/h H 2 , B10 blend) achieved a maximum Brake Thermal Efficiency of 31.2% and 10–15% lower Brake Specific Fuel Consumption under high‐load conditions. Moreover, this hydrogen‐enriched RCCI mode achieved average reductions in CO, HC, NOx, and smoke emissions of 24%, 27%, 35%, and 40%, respectively. title: Design of a direct-drive axle-mounted traction motor for boosting high-speed trains
abstract: Background High-speed railway traction systems must combine high efficiency and power density within constrained mechanical envelopes. This work presents the design and numerical assessment of a direct-drive permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) for supplementary traction, designed to fit between the wheel and axlebox of an existing high-speed train while retaining its disc-brake hardware. Methods The design methodology combines multiobjective parametric optimisation with topology optimisation to limit magnetic flux leakage while preserving manufacturability. An oil-flooded, slot-through cooling system was integrated into the motor. Electromagnetic, thermal and structural simulations assessed nominal operation, fault conditions, overspeed, shock and vibration loads derived from railway standards. High-speed-boost and load-sharing strategies were benchmarked over a representative duty cycle against the reference geared induction-motor powertrain. title: Experimental and machine-learning based investigation of second generation juliflora biodiesel blended with dimethyl carbonate and CoCr 2 O 4 nanoparticles in a compression ignition engine
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part C Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science
abstract: Improving the efficiency and emission characteristics of biodiesel fueled CI engine remains challenging due to limitations in fuel reactivity and combustion behavior. This study investigates the combined effect of dimethyl carbonate (DMC) and cobalt chromite nanoparticles on engine performance and emissions, supported by machine learning-based prediction. Experiments were carried out on a single-cylinder diesel engine using five fuel blends including diesel, J20, J20D10, J20D10C50, and J20D10C100 across the full load range. The J20D10C100 blend delivered the highest BTE of 29.67%, showing improvements of 13.57% over diesel and 20.78% over the J20 blend. Brake specific fuel consumption decreased to 0.375 kg per kWh, corresponding to reductions of 5.44% and 6.38% compared with diesel and the J20 blend. At full load, CO decreased from 0.53% to 0.454%, HC reduced by 14.6%, and nitrogen oxides decreased from 1070 ppm to 990 ppm. Smoke opacity showed a reduction from 67.21% to 65.19%. Among the predictive models, gradient boosting achieved the highest accuracy with an R 2 of 0.965, followed closely by random forest with 0.964. The results confirm that the proposed fuel formulation enhances engine performance while reducing emissions, which supports reliable predictive modeling.

title: Extremely Low Mass Ratio Contact Binaries. III. Photometric and Spectroscopic Investigations of 11 Systems
abstract: Abstract We present photometric and spectroscopic investigations of 11 totally eclipsing contact binaries with mass ratios below 0.15, classifying them as extremely low mass ratio contact binaries. The ground-based multiband light curves were modeled with PHysics Of Eclipsing BinariEs to derive the photometric parameters of these systems. The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) light curves of J011323 and J002747 show pronounced asymmetries and continuous variations. Markov Chain Monte Carlo modeling suggests that these variations are related to longitudinal migration of spots on the primary components. Spectral subtraction of the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) spectra reveals excess chromospheric emission in six systems, while no detectable excess emission is found in the other five. The O − C analysis indicates secular period increases in six systems and secular decreases in five systems. We estimated their orbital angular momenta and performed a dynamical analysis. Within our adopted semianalytical framework without energy transfer, the formation of these observed systems requires additional angular momentum loss beyond saturated magnetic braking and gravitational radiation, but this requirement could be modified by different assumptions on mass transfer or radius evolution.

title: Synergistic Regulation of Common Rail Pressure and Injection Angle on Heavy‐Duty Diesel Engine Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates a commercial heavy‐duty diesel engine equipped with a DOC + DPF + SCR + ASC aftertreatment system, which already meets China VI emission standards. Through coordinated optimization experiments of injection timing and common‐rail pressure under typical operating conditions, the comprehensive effects of injection parameters on the power performance, fuel economy, emission characteristics, and vibration levels of the engine are systematically studied. The results indicate that increasing common rail pressure enhances the power performance of heavy‐duty diesel engines: when the injection timing is maintained constant at 5°CA before top dead center (BTDC) and the rail pressure is gradually increased from 100 MPa to 130 MPa in 10 MPa increments, the engine's torque and power increase continuously with rising rail pressure, specifically increasing from 1330.5 N·m and 166.8 kW (at 100 MPa) to 1368.1 N·m and 177.0 kW (at 130 MPa), respectively. However, the influence of injection advance angle on power performance does not exhibit a monotonic positive correlation; instead, an optimal injection advance angle exists. title: A Data Analysis and Comparison of Traditional and Alternative Powertrains in Motorsport
abstract: Motorsport has depended on internal combustion engines (ICEs) for decades, but growing concerns about energy efficiency and environmental impact have increased interest in alternative powertrain technologies. This paper compares internal combustion engine (ICE), battery-electric vehicle (BEV), and hydrogen fuel-cell electric vehicle (FCEV) powertrains in motorsport. The three powertrains are evaluated according to well-to-wheels and powertrain efficiency, energy replenishment, environmental impact, economic factors, and regulatory development. Published data are collected and analyzed to quantify well-to-wheels energy consumption, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and thermodynamic efficiency, with comparisons also made between motorsport and conventional vehicles to examine how the distinct performance requirements of motorsport affect powertrain efficiency and environmental impact. For the selected racing cases, BEVs and FCEVs exhibit approximately 42.4% and 47.6% of the WTW energy consumption of ICEs, respectively, while their estimated WTW GHG emissions are 21.5% and 3.25% of those of ICEs under the selected upstream energy pathways. The analysis shows that ICEs offer well-proven high-performance characteristics and fast refueling, but they have a lower energy-conversion efficiency and produce direct GHG emissions. title: Enabling High-Efficiency Spark-Ignited Natural Gas Engines via Variable Valve Actuation and In-Cylinder Sensing
abstract: Stringent greenhouse gas and criteria pollutant regulations for medium- and heavy-duty vehicles have accelerated the adoption of cleaner engine technologies. While zero-emission solutions are growing, the widespread deployment of internal combustion engines powered by alternative fuels remains essential in the near term. title: Experimental study on lean combustion in an ammonia engine with a hydrogen pre-chamber
abstract: Hydrogen pre-chamber ammonia engines are a promising zero‑carbon engine concept for transportation decarbonization. However, they still face two key challenges: first, at low loads, the minimum hydrogen energy ratio (HER) required for stable combustion, denoted as mHER, is relatively high; second, improvements in brake thermal efficiency (BTE) at high loads are limited by heat-transfer losses. Given the flow communication between the main chamber and the pre-chamber through the jet orifices, changes in main-chamber mixture leanness are expected to alter the oxygen availability of the mixture entering the pre-chamber, thereby affecting pre-chamber reactivity, jet characteristics, and subsequent main-chamber combustion. Experiments were conducted under various combinations of load, excess air ratio (λ), and HER. The experimental results demonstrate that appropriately increasing main-chamber mixture leanness accelerates the combustion of the pre-chamber mixture and strengthens jets, thereby promoting faster main-chamber combustion, higher BTE, and lower mHER. However, excessively lean ammonia-air mixtures in the main chamber were more difficult to ignite, burned more slowly, and were more susceptible to quenching, thereby increasing the mHER and unburned ammonia emissions. abstract: Modernization and conversion of agricultural machinery to alternative fuels is a key tool for improv-ing its environmental and economic performance. The purpose of the work is to develop methods and techniques for experimental research of a diesel engine in a gasodiesel cycle, which ensures its stable operation at various load-speed modes with different fuel mixture compositions.
